standard_prerequisites.name: The reduction of injectivity over a ring epimorphism to injectivity over the source ring
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked at the start of the counted proof (source lines 534-536)
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the claim about the localized module to the claim that it is injective as a module over the original ring.

standard_prerequisites.name: Baer's criterion for injectivity of a module
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source line 537)
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces injectivity to extending maps out of ideals.

standard_prerequisites.name: The lifting of a map out of a finitely presented module after inverting an element of the multiplicative subset
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof (source lines 540-543)
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the element of the multiplicative subset and the map into the original module whose composition is the given map.

core_obligations: Reduce the ring: since the localization map is an epimorphism of rings it suffices to test injectivity of the localized module over the original Noetherian ring (proof lines 534-536)
Apply Baer's criterion: take an ideal and a map from it into the localized module (proof lines 537-539)

Lift and extend: finite presentation of the ideal in a Noetherian ring gives an element of the multiplicative subset and a map from the ideal into the original injective module which composes to the given map after inverting that element; extend this map to the whole ring by injectivity and compose with the inverse of the element to obtain the required extension (proof lines 540-549)
proof_roadmap: R → S^{-1}R 是环满射 ⇒ 只需证 S^{-1}E 作为 R-模内射（injective-epimorphism）。
用 Baer 判别法：取理想 I ⊂ R 与映射 φ: I → S^{-1}E。
R Noetherian ⇒ I 有限表现 ⇒ 存在 f ∈ S 与 I → E 使 fφ 为 I → E → S^{-1}E（同 from-finitely-presented）；把 I → E 延拓到 R → E，再复合 f^{-1} 即得 φ 的延拓 ⇒ S^{-1}E 内射。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement says that for a Noetherian ring and a multiplicative subset the localization of an injective module is injective over the localized ring (author lemma at source lines 526-531, label lemma-localization-injective-modules). The proof (source lines 533-550) reduces to injectivity over the original ring through the ring epimorphism, applies Baer's criterion, and uses finite presentation of an ideal in a Noetherian ring to lift a map into the localized module to a map into the original injective module after inverting one element, which is then extended over the whole ring and divided by that element (proof lines 540-549). The lifting step is the substance. H3.
